title: Absolute value
competency: Find the absolute value of a real number and the distance between two real numbers.

keywords.def: The distance of a number from 0 on the number line: |x| is never negative.

keywords.am: በ a እና b መካከል ያለ ርቀት
keywords.def: The distance between two real numbers a and b is |a − b|, and |a − b| = |b − a|.

en.text: The absolute value of x, written |x|, is its distance from 0. It is never negative. If x is 0 or positive, |x| = x. If x is negative, |x| = −x. The distance between a and b is |a − b|.

am.text: የ x ፍጹም ዋጋ |x| ተብሎ ይጻፋል። ከዜሮ ያለው ርቀት ነው፤ አሉታዊ አይሆንም። x አዎንታዊ ወይም ዜሮ ከሆነ |x| = x ነው። x አሉታዊ ከሆነ |x| = −x ነው። በ a እና b መካከል ያለው ርቀት |a − b| ነው።

screens.title: Who walked farther?
screens.text: Bekele walks 3 km west of Meskel Square. Tigist walks 3 km east of it. Call east positive: Bekele is at −3, Tigist at 3.
screens.ask: Who is farther from Meskel Square?
screens.after:
Both are 3 km from Meskel Square.
Direction does not change distance: |−3| = |3| = 3.
The book calls this absolute value.

screens.title: Definition 1.8
paras: The absolute value of a real number x is written |x|.
|x| = x if x ≥ 0, and |x| = −x if x < 0.
It is the distance of x from 0. So it is never negative.

screens.title: Distance from 0
screens.ask: Tap each point. The arc shows its distance from 0.

points.info: Bekele is 3 km from the square.
A positive number is its own absolute value.

screens.title: Absolute value
defs: |x| is the distance of x from 0. |x| = x if x ≥ 0, and |x| = −x if x < 0.

screens.title: Find the distance from 0
screens.why:
|x| is the distance of x from 0.
−0.4 is 0.4 units left of 0.
So |−0.4| = 0.4.
−0.4 is wrong: an absolute value is never negative.
screens.clue: How far is −0.4 from 0 on the number line?

screens.text: Absolute values of some real numbers.

screens.title: Careful with roots
screens.text: Absolute value of a difference: what is |3 − √10|?
screens.why:
First find the sign: √10 ≈ 3.16, which is more than 3.
So 3 − √10 ≈ −0.16 is negative.
For negative x, |x| = −x.
|3 − √10| = −(3 − √10) = √10 − 3.

screens.title: Distance between two numbers
paras: Example 2: The distance between −3 and 4 is 7 units.
The distance between a and b is |a − b|, and |a − b| = |b − a|.
screens.note: Figure 1.8: drag a and b on the number line; the distance |a − b| never goes negative.

screens.title: From −3 to 4
screens.ask: Tap Hop. How far is it from −3 to 4?
screens.after:
The hop is 7 units long.
|−3 − 4| = |−7| = 7 and |4 − (−3)| = |7| = 7.
The order does not matter.

screens.title: Distance on the line
defs: |a − b|. The order does not matter: |a − b| = |b − a|.

screens.title: Find a distance
screens.ask: Distance on the line: the distance between −5 and 2 is ___.
screens.why:
Distance = |a − b|.
|−5 − 2| = |−7|.
|−7| = 7.
Check by counting: 5 steps from −5 to 0, then 2 more: 7.
screens.clue: Subtract one number from the other, then take the absolute value.

screens.title: Solve |x| = 5
screens.why:
|x| = 5 means x is 5 units from 0.
Go 5 right: x = 5. Go 5 left: x = −5.
Both work: |5| = 5 and |−5| = 5.
So x = 5 or x = −5.
screens.clue: Which numbers are 5 units from zero?

screens.title: A cold morning
screens.text: One morning in Debre Berhan it is −2 °C. By noon it is 9 °C.
screens.ask: Find the rise: the temperature rose by ___ °C.
screens.why:
Rise = distance from −2 to 9.
|9 − (−2)| = |9 + 2| = |11|.
|11| = 11.
The temperature rose by 11 °C.

items.why:
|x| is the distance from 0.
−3/4 is 3/4 units left of 0.
So |−3/4| = 3/4 (= 0.75).

items.text: Absolute value of a difference: find |1 − √2|.
items.why:
√2 ≈ 1.41, which is more than 1.
So 1 − √2 ≈ −0.41 is negative.
For negative x, |x| = −x.
|1 − √2| = −(1 − √2) = √2 − 1.

items.ask: Distance on the line: the distance between 7 and −9 is ___.

items.why:
|x| is a distance, so it is never negative.
No number has an absolute value of −4.
So there is no solution.
x = −4 is wrong: |−4| = 4, not −4.

First get |x| alone: subtract 3 from both sides.
|x| = 14 − 3 = 11.
x is 11 units from 0.
So x = 11 or x = −11.

items.text: The coldest temperature recorded on Earth is −129 °F, at Vostok Station, Antarctica, in 1983. The book gives the hottest as 136 °F at Al'Aziziyah, Libya.
items.ask: Find the range with the book's figures: ___ °F.
items.why:
Range = highest − lowest.
136 − (−129) = 136 + 129.
136 + 129 = 265 °F.
Note: the 136 °F reading was ruled invalid in 2012.
With the official 134 °F (Death Valley), the range is 134 + 129 = 263 °F.
items.clue: Range = highest − lowest. Subtracting a negative adds.

test.text: Absolute value of a difference: what is |2 − √8|?
test.why:
√8 ≈ 2.83, which is more than 2.
So 2 − √8 is negative.
|2 − √8| = −(2 − √8) = √8 − 2.
2 − √8 is wrong: an absolute value is never negative.

test.ask: Distance on the line: the distance between −49 and −100 is ___.

test.text: True or false? The equation |x| = 0 has exactly one solution.
test.why:
|x| = 0 means x is 0 units from 0.
Only x = 0 does that.
So there is exactly one solution: true.

screens.title: Subtract a negative
screens.text: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.why:
Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.
9 − (−2) = 9 + 2.
9 + 2 = 11.
7 is a slip: it subtracts 2 instead of adding.
